What is Andi?

Small independent, privacy-first AI search engine that answers conversationally and strips ads, trackers and clutter from results. Positions itself as a calm, safe alternative to mainstream search.

Best for

Private, ad-free everyday search with clean reading.

Main features

  • Conversational answers with sources
  • ad-free and tracker-free by design
  • no user profiling or search history retention
  • reader mode that extracts clean article text
  • summarise-any-page function
  • visual search results
  • kid-safe filtering.

Practical use cases

  • Everyday search without ad tracking
  • reading long articles distraction-free
  • safe search for classrooms and families
  • quick summarisation of a URL.

Who is it for?

  • Privacy-conscious individuals, students, educators, parents and users on low-bandwidth connections.

Pricing, free access & limits

Free product; no published paid tier

Plans described in the source

Free. No paid subscription published as of the check date. The team has historically funded development through grants and small-scale support rather than subscriptions.

Free plan

Yes - the entire product is free.

Free trial

n/a

Usage limits to consider

No published hard limits; fair-use rate limiting applies. Capability is well below frontier assistants.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Genuinely no ads and no tracking
  • very fast and lightweight
  • clean reader mode is excellent
  • safe for classroom use
  • free with no account required.

Limitations to consider

  • Much weaker reasoning and synthesis than Perplexity or ChatGPT
  • small index and limited freshness
  • no API
  • tiny team means uncertain long-term viability
  • little non-English depth.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web, iOS, Android, Chrome extension

Languages

  • Primarily English; other languages handled but less reliably

API access

No public API published

Integrations and exports

  • Browser extension
  • set as default search engine

Evaluation notes

Best treated as a privacy-respecting search front end rather than a research assistant. Confirm the project is still actively maintained before standardising on it.
